info.name: kagent on EKS: controller API, tool server, agents
info.description:
The kagent controller's HTTP API (port 8083), the built-in tool server's MCP endpoint (port 8084), and the agents of this build, all through kubectl port-forwards:

    kubectl -n kagent port-forward svc/kagent-controller 8083:8083
    kubectl -n kagent port-forward svc/kagent-tools 8084:8084
    kubectl -n kagent port-forward svc/netprobe-mcp 3002:3000

Authentication: the controller runs in its default `unsecure` mode. It takes the user from `?user_id=` or the `X-User-Id` header and otherwise uses `admin@kagent.dev`. No request is rejected. Sessions are filtered by that user.

Routes were read from kagent v0.9.10 `go/core/internal/httpserver/server.go`. Most responses are wrapped as `{error, data, message}`.

variable.description: agent name for the A2A and session requests

item.name: 1 · System
item.description: Routes that need no body. /health and /version skip authentication.

request.description: `{error:false, data:{status:'OK'}}`. handlers/health.go
`{kagent_version, git_commit, build_date}`; not wrapped. server.go:219
In unsecure mode returns `{sub: '<user id>'}` for the resolved user. Try it with `?user_id=someone@example.com` to see the fallback logic.
`[{name, status}]` for every namespace the controller can see.

item.name: 2 · Model configs
item.description: A ModelConfig is kagent's 'model an agent can use'. Every one in this build points at OpenRouter through its OpenAI-compatible API and reads the key from the Secret `kagent-openrouter`. handlers/modelconfig.go

request.description: `[{ref: 'ns/name', spec, status}]`.

item.name: create model config (API instead of YAML)

request.description: Same result as `kubectl apply` of a ModelConfig. `ref` is `namespace/name`. Optional `apiKey` creates the Secret for you; here the existing Secret is referenced instead. `defaultHeaders` are sent on every LLM request (OpenRouter uses HTTP-Referer and X-Title for attribution). Returns 201.
Body is `{spec, apiKey?, secrets?}`; the whole spec is replaced.
`[{name, type, requiredParams, optionalParams}]`: the providers kagent knows and what each needs.
A hardcoded provider→models map used by the UI's dropdowns (handlers/models.go). OpenRouter models are not in it; any model id works in a ModelConfig regardless.

item.name: 3 · Tool servers and tools
item.description: Tool sources kagent knows: RemoteMCPServer resources (a URL), MCPServer resources (run by kmcp), and Services labelled `kagent.dev/mcp-service: "true"`. The controller connects to each, lists its tools and stores them. handlers/toolservers.go, handlers/tools.go

item.name: list tool servers with their discovered tools

request.description: `[{ref, groupKind, discoveredTools: [{name, description}]}]`. The built-in server `kagent/kagent-tool-server` lists 124 tools.
`[{id, server_name, group_kind, description, ...}]`. `id` is the MCP tool name. No input schema here; get that from the server itself (folder 4).

item.name: register a RemoteMCPServer through the API

request.description: Body: `{type, remoteMCPServer | mcpServer, secrets?}`. Equivalent to applying the RemoteMCPServer YAML.

item.name: 4 · Call the built-in tools directly (no LLM)
item.description: `kubectl -n kagent port-forward svc/kagent-tools 8084:8084`. The tool server is a plain MCP server over streamable HTTP, with no authentication. These requests are what an agent's runtime does when the model asks for a tool. Argument names are from `tools/list`; check them there if a call returns an error, since the tool server (kagent-tools 0.2.1) is not part of the kagent source.

request.description: Standard MCP handshake against the tool server itself (`kagent-tools`, port 8084). The test script stores the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header for the following requests.
Second half of the handshake. Expect HTTP 202 with an empty body.
Every tool with its description and `inputSchema`. This is where the argument names for the calls below come from.
The same data `kubectl get pods -A -o wide` returns, as text.
Events of the namespace with the deliberately broken workloads.
Replace the pod name with one from the first call.
Helm releases in the cluster.

Needs the kube-prometheus-stack from the setup guide monitoring step. The tool rejects comparison operators (`>`, `<`, `==`) as "potentially dangerous characters", so filter with topk() instead of `> 0`.

item.name: 5 · Agents
item.description: An Agent is one YAML resource: description, type (Declarative or BYO), model config, system message, tools. The API takes and returns the same object `kubectl` does. handlers/agents.go

request.description: `[{id, agent: {spec, status...}, modelProvider, model, tools, deploymentReady, accepted}]`. `deploymentReady` and `accepted` are what the UI shows as the agent's health.

item.name: create an agent through the API

request.description: The body is a full `kagent.dev/v1alpha2` Agent object. The controller creates the Deployment and Service for it; `deploymentReady` turns true after about a minute. Returns 201.

item.name: update the agent (PUT, no path params)

request.description: PUT has no namespace/name in the path; they come from `metadata`. Only `spec` is replaced.

item.name: 6 · Invoke an agent (A2A)
item.description: Agents are invoked over the A2A protocol at `/api/a2a/{ns}/{name}/`: JSON-RPC 2.0, method `message/send`. The controller forwards to the agent pod and returns a Task whose `status.state` is `completed`, `failed`, `working` or `input-required` (waiting for a human). Without an `A2A-Version` header the wire format is A2A 0.3 (lowercase states); with `A2A-Version: 1.0` the v1 format. a2a/a2a_handler_mux.go

request.description: Built by the controller from the Agent resource: name, description, skills, and the URL callers should use.

One JSON-RPC call; the agent's whole tool loop runs behind it (30 s to 2 min). The test script stores `task_id` and `session_id` (= `contextId`) and prints the answer. Set the `agent` variable to try the other agents.

item.name: 3 · message/send · follow-up in the same session

request.description: Same `contextId` = same session: the agent sees the previous turn.
The stored task with its history and artifacts.

item.name: 5 · sre-operator · a change that needs approval

request.description: `sre-operator` lists `k8s_scale` in `requireApproval`. Expect `status.state: input-required`: the runtime emitted an `adk_request_confirmation` call and is waiting. The pending call is in the task's last message as a data part.

Approval is another `message/send` on the same `contextId` and `taskId`, with a data part `{decision_type: approve}` (or `reject`, optionally with `rejection_reason`). This is what the UI's Approve button sends (ui/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx). The task then continues and completes.

This request explicitly targets sre-orchestrator, regardless of the `agent` variable. The default question is scenario 14, which completed in the recorded build. `message/stream` returns server-sent events as the agent works: status updates (delegated calls appear as function-call data parts), artifact updates with the answer, and a final status. In kagent 0.9.10 the controller cuts both `message/send` and `message/stream` at 180 seconds; streaming exposes progress but does not bypass that timeout. This request does not automatically save task/session IDs: for continuation, copy the latest result.taskId and result.contextId from the events into `task_id` and `session_id`.
Same call, v1 wire format: the response uses `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`-style enums.

item.name: 7 · Sessions and tasks
item.description: A session is a conversation with one agent; its id is the A2A `contextId`. The UI creates one per chat. handlers/sessions.go, handlers/tasks.go

request.description: `agent_ref` is required. The returned `id` is used as `contextId` in A2A messages. The test script stores it.
Filtered by user. The UI's chats are here too, under `admin@kagent.dev`.
`{session, events: [...]}`. Each event's `data` is a JSON-encoded A2A message: user turns, tool calls, tool results, agent text.

item.name: 8 · The controller's own MCP endpoint (agents as tools)
item.description: The controller serves an MCP server at `/mcp` on port 8083 with two tools: `list_agents` and `invoke_agent`. Any MCP client, or another agent, can use kagent agents as tools this way. internal/mcp/mcp_handler.go

request.description: Server name is `kagent-agents`. Stateful unless the controller runs with KAGENT_MCP_STATELESS=true, so keep the session header.
Expect `list_agents` and `invoke_agent`.
Only agents that are accepted and whose deployment is ready are listed.
Runs an A2A message/send behind the scenes and returns the agent's text plus `{agent, text, context_id}`.

item.name: 9 · Feedback
item.description: Thumbs up/down on an agent message, as the UI does. handlers/feedback.go

request.description: `feedback_text` is required; `issue_type` is one of instructions, factual, incomplete, tool.
